transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-12
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Brooks (Redwood SE), Liam Chen (Redwood CSM), Jared Kim (Cobalt Lead Eng), Priya Desai (Cobalt PM), Lena Ortiz (Cobalt Security), Marco Villar (Cobalt SRE)
Linked artifacts: Drive: https://redwood.internal/pilots/cobalt-health/benchmarks, Deck: https://redwood.app/deck/pilot-kickoff, Perf spreadsheet: https://redwood.app/sheets/pilot-benchmarks

Summary (auto): quick sync to review last week's POC results on SDK integration, function calling serialization issues, and next steps to harden structured output acceptance. Focus: reproduce two failing cases, finalize SDK retry patterns, confirm security gating for private deployment.

Transcript:
[00:00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for carving out time, we'll run about 45 minutes, go through the recent test results and nail down action items. you all good with that?
[00:00:12] Jared: yeah sounds good, busy week but we got the test harness results that I uploaded, see the sheet link in the chat.
[00:00:20] Priya: quick thing on agenda, we want to make sure SDK error semantics are stable before we move to staging, and the serialization mismatch is the blocker.
[00:00:28] Ethan: cool, I can start with a short recap of the failing scenarios and what we changed last sprint.
[00:00:35] Ethan: so two main failures: one is the function-calling payload that occasionally drops the metadata field when there's a nested list, second is an edge case where the structured output contains trailing commas and our parser in the app rejects it. we saw the first failure about 8% of requests under load in your sandbox traces.
[00:00:52] Marco: that 8% number, is that with prefix caching enabled? we toggled cache on to emulate production.
[00:01:00] Ethan: yeah that run had KV cache on and batching at 32ms windows. we also tried a run with cache off and the failure dropped to 1.2% so there's an interaction there.
[00:01:12] Maya: ok that's helpful. Jared, do you have the example payloads for the failing case?
[00:01:18] Jared: yep uploaded — in the sheet rows 42-53. but note, some of the IDs are masked, so if you need original keys I can share a sanitized dump.
[00:01:28] Ethan: the interesting bit is the metadata field is sometimes merged into the previous token boundary during decoder streaming, looks like a stream boundary/regeneration artifact, might be our continuous batching edge.
[00:01:40] Priya: so is this a model behavior or SDK reassembly issue? we need to know for our roadmap decision (hosted vs dedicated).
[00:01:48] Ethan: early signal is the SDK reassembly of function call chunks — when response arrives as two streamed chunks, our client-side join logic attempted to merge JSON fragments and lost the nested list key in a race. we pushed a fix to the SDK patch that enforces strict chunk-join ordering and re-parses.
[00:02:03] Maya: and we'll share that patch today in the repo link. Ethan, do you want to mention the retry semantics we recommend?
[00:02:09] Ethan: sure. recommended pattern: idempotent function calls should use incremental backoff with the SDK's built-in idempotency token; also validate JSON shape server-side and if mismatch return 412 with the raw token attached so client can replay deterministically. we'll add sample snippets in the repo.
[00:02:26] Lena: on the security side we're worried about replaying tokens outside the VPC, and KMS keys — we need to confirm whether Redwood can support customer-managed keys for the pilot.
[00:02:36] Maya: yes, we support CMKs in Private deployments; for Hosted we can do envelope encryption with BYOK via KMS in the new flow. I'll send the SOC2 and KMS docs.
[00:02:47] Lena: great. also need audit log granularity — can we get token-level traces with redaction?
[00:02:52] Liam: we can provide redacted token-level traces; we have a tooling pipeline that strips PII and retains call IDs. we'll add an example export.
[00:03:00] Marco: back to perf — when you turned off cache the failure dropped but latency increased, so there's a tradeoff. any guidance on safe caching knobs?
[00:03:08] Ethan: yes, our suggestion: enable prefix-only KV cache for critical calls (cache keys based solely on prefix hash), keep batching windows small (15-20ms) for low-latency critical paths, and use adaptive batching for background workloads. also, quantization on model variant reduces token compute and slightly reduces burst failure surface.
[00:03:28] Priya: do you have numbers for latency uplift when turning cache off?
[00:03:33] Ethan: in your traces median p99 went from 180ms to 240ms when cache off under your test load. cost per token rose about 12% in that run.
[00:03:44] Jared: for our SLAs, 240ms p99 is borderline, so we want to avoid full cache disable. maybe we can tune to prefix-only cache as you suggested.
[00:03:52] Maya: sounds like action item: Redwood SE to run targeted test with prefix-only cache + chunked streaming patch and send results. Ethan?
[00:04:00] Ethan: yes will do, I plan two test permutations and will upload traces.
[00:04:04] Priya: second topic: structured output validation — our app rejects when parser sees trailing commas or unescaped linefeeds. is there a recommended schema approach?
[00:04:15] Ethan: we recommend function-calling with JSON-schema enforced on the model side and a last-resort sanitizer in the SDK that attempts to auto-fix minor deviations (strip trailing commas, normalize newlines) but only if safe; otherwise fail fast and return raw buffer for replay.
[00:04:31] Marco: won't auto-fixing mask latent bugs in prompt design?
[00:04:36] Ethan: good point — sanitizer is opt-in. best practice is to iterate the prompt and tests until model emits schema-compliant output, sanitizer only for non-blocking production traffic with explicit monitoring.
[00:04:46] Lena: for compliance we prefer fail-fast so we can audit failure reasons. the auto-fix approach complicates audit trails.
[00:04:53] Maya: noted — we'll default to fail-fast and provide a telemetry hook that logs the raw failing output to the audit pipeline with redaction.
[00:05:00] Priya: on SDK ergonomics, our engineers requested a higher-level helper that validates and throws typed errors for missing keys instead of raw parsing exceptions.
[00:05:09] Ethan: we can add a utility: validateFunctionResponse(response, schema) -> typed error class. will include sample in the patch.
[00:05:16] Jared: one weird thing we saw, sometimes the function call name gets mangled in the streaming case — we get "function_name": "upsert_user" sometimes becomes "upset_user" (typo) during assembly.
[00:05:27] Ethan: that's likely tokenization splitting the underscore across chunks. patch will ensure underscore tokens are preserved in reassembly.
[00:05:34] Priya: lovely, thanks. quick question about dedicated vs hosted: if we go dedicated for predictability, how much lead time and what are minimum commitments?
[00:05:44] Maya: dedicated typically requires a monthly commit for the pool — minimum three month initial term for pilot in most cases. lead time varies by region, usually 2-3 weeks if we have capacity. for strict compliance (air-gapped) we'd do Private on-prem which is longer.
[00:06:00] Marco: and cost differential? rough order of magnitude?
[00:06:03] Maya: Dedicated is a fixed monthly for the reserved GPUs plus usage; generally 20-35% cheaper at scale versus hosted bursts for sustained throughput. we'll share a tailored quote once we have your expected QPS profile.
[00:06:16] Lena: before budget we need to confirm audit controls and whether private deployment supports our HSM.
[00:06:21] Maya: yes Private supports HSM/KMS integrations; we'll loop in our Security Solutions engineer to confirm specifics.
[00:06:28] Ethan: another small note — we saw a couple of 500s in the run tied to model reloads during a canary deploy. we recommend enabling rolling canaries with graceful drain hooks to minimize in-flight request failures.
[00:06:40] Jared: can you share the canary config example? we need to match our deploy orchestrator.
[00:06:44] Ethan: will attach a sample helm/patch snippet to the repo.
[00:06:48] Priya: let's recap next steps before we close.
[00:06:51] Maya: recap: Redwood to share SDK patch and sample snippets (today), SE to run prefix-only cache+patch perf test (by 1/15), Redwood to send SOC2 + KMS + audit docs (by 1/14), Customer to share failing payloads and reconciled expected schema (by 1/18), schedule deep dive on KV cache behavior (target 1/20).
[00:07:12] Jared: that matches our notes. thanks.
[00:07:16] Lena: one last ask — can you include an example of redaction rules for token-level traces so we can review?
[00:07:21] Liam: yes, will include a redaction policy example.
[00:07:25] Maya: awesome, thanks everyone. we'll follow up in the thread with the links.
[00:07:29] (call ends)

Quality notes: transcription occasionally merged tokens and mis-spelled underscores; speaker labels are accurate for the AE/SE pair but sometimes generic in short interjections.
